name: CA-16
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+25 district lean in the Bay Area
First-term incumbent with no outside opposition spending
model.rationale: The D+25 district, Liccardo's overwhelming financial advantage, and markets pricing him near certain re-election all point to a Safe D race with no evidence of a competitive general election.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending against Liccardo would be the first sign of a real contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Sam Liccardo, a first-term Democratic incumbent, defends a San Jose-area seat with a Democratic partisan lean of 25 points. He advanced to the general against Republican Peter Soule, who has raised only about $400,000 and has no outside support, while Liccardo has raised nearly $3.5 million and holds over $2 million on hand. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent.

Prediction markets put Liccardo's chances around 97 percent, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's strong Democratic lean, the incumbent's financial dominance, and the absence of any reported signs of a real contest, all pointing to a comfortable Liccardo re-election.
